anomalies.observed: Both ground pins on each CAN isolation transceiver are connected to the same GND net: U10.4 (GND1) and U10.5 (GND2), and U11.4 (GND1) and U11.5 (GND2).
anomalies.expected: The logic-side and bus-side grounds must remain separate for the CAN interfaces to provide galvanic isolation, as intended by the specification's description of two isolated CAN buses using isolated CAN transceivers.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The shared ground bypasses the transceivers' isolation barrier, so the CAN interfaces are not galvanically isolated and will not provide the intended separation from bus-side ground faults or common-mode voltage.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: each CAN transceiver's logic-side and bus-side ground pins are tied to the same GND net. This defeats the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces.
